newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha falls on crude, ends bull run.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha falls on crude, ends bull run.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices fell on Tuesday ending a five-day bull run, in reaction to a sharp fall in overseas crude oil markets, traders said.
"Naphtha finally followed crude oil," one trader said.
Naphtha prices continued to rise for the last five business days in Tokyo, shrugging off fluctuations in overseas crude markets, which usually provide direction for Asian naphtha markets.
Thailand's recent purchases of prompt cargoes were said to have supported the Tokyo market's rise.
Second-half September open-spec naphtha was quoted at $204.25/$205.00 per tonne. It was traded at $207.00 on Monday.
Open-spec naphtha is Asia's benchmark forward contract for naphtha trading.
Naphtha spreads remained in backwardation in quiet talks, with first-half September/first-half October roughly assessed at plus $1.00/$1.50.

In low sulphur waxy residue trading, Indonesian cargoes were quoted above $2.00 per barrel over the Pertamina formula after some July spot cargoes were said to be traded at premiums of around $2.05, traders said. --Tokyo Energy Desk
